time_convention: t = frame / fps, frame 0 at t = 0; frame = round(t * fps)
units: pixels (full resolution, x right, y down) and seconds; no metric scale assumed
description: Static top-down (near-nadir) drone view of a red hard tennis court in low sun with long shadows toward upper-left. Near half of the court (baseline at top, y~870) to net (y~2870) plus the far half down to the frame bottom (far service line and far baseline are off-frame). Two players on the near half: the right player runs down-court toward the net and volleys/hits the ball at frame ~37.8; the left player stands still holding a racket. The ball enters from the lower part (already in flight at frame 0, rising after a bounce just before the clip), is hit by the right player and flies down-right over the net, leaving the bottom of the frame after frame 91.

camera.evidence: phase correlation of every frame vs frame 0: |shift| <= 0.7 px over all 111 frames (sub-pixel jitter, no pan/zoom)
camera.view: near-nadir top-down; slight perspective: court sidelines converge slightly toward the top (doubles width 1786 px at y=900 vs 1830 px at y=3800, ~2.5%), baseline tilted ~0.35 deg (y 864.5 at x=300, 875 at x=1950)
camera.ground_plane: court surface = image plane to within ~2.5 % scale variation over the frame; airborne ball is above the plane (its cast shadow on the court is tracked separately)
